guard: `cotal run` refuses an unroutable verb as a usage error before any plane opens, and every verb the gate routes is a declared run subcommand or alias
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/run-command-usage.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd
why: The unknown-verb case supplies both answer positionals and invalid JSON, so the verb gate must answer before the answer arity or the value check. Without the gate the verb still reaches a usage refusal, but one that names the arity rather than the declared commands, so the cell grades the gate's own sentence.

mutations.name: the verb gate is gone, so an unroutable verb reaches the per-verb arity checks
mutations.find: if (extra.length || !["start", "resume", "ps", "journal", "answer", "amend", "revoke", "migrate", "validate", "plan", "simulate", "turns", "yield"].includes(verb)) usage("choose a declared run command; run it bare to list workflows");
mutations.replace: if (extra.length) usage("choose a declared run command; run it bare to list workflows");
mutations.expectRed: an unknown verb is refused as a usage error before any plane is opened
mutations.cell: an unknown verb is refused as a usage error before any plane is opened
mutations.note: Re-anchored for the redesign, which moved the gate from the dispatcher's usage print into workflowArguments. Without the list check, `frobnicate run-0 <step>` falls through to the one-identifier arity rule and is refused with a sentence that does not name the declared commands. The validate-hook cell goes red with it, since the hook calls the same grammar.

mutations.name: the declaration loses a verb the gate still routes
mutations.note: The two lists drift independently; this is the drift the loop of declared-verb cells exists to catch. Re-anchored for the redesign, which moved the verbs from the usage line into the command's subcommand declaration, where `ps` is the hidden list subcommand's alias.
